question: Does the split-sample selection procedure of docs/plans/2026-08-27-option-set-comparison-spec.md section 2.4 actually recover a planted effect? The seven registered policies of the option-set pilot are run unchanged, plus one eighth arm (wt-doubled) that is the wt-free control with Watchtower damage doubled from 3 to 6 via balanceOverrides. The procedure must select that arm as the best in the full set on BOTH mazes. This family measures the instrument, not the game: it issues no balance verdict about any policy or fusion.
sigmaSource: Identical to option-set-pilot (test/harness/prereg/option-set-pilot.json), reused deliberately so this check runs at the SAME power as the family it validates: paired hallHpAuc delta sd measured in the R2 regime by regime-r2-adoption (docs/reviews/2026-08-15-regime-r2-adoption.md, 24,000 runs, 18/18 gates PASS), ~0.87 (maze A) / ~1.41 (maze B), maze B binding. mde(sigma/sqrt(2), 750) = 0.089 (A) / 0.144 (B) at 750 seed-cells per split side, where 750 is the size of EACH of the two random halves (S1 selection, S2 evaluation) that the 1500 seed-cells per arm per maze (750 seeds x 2 postGaps) are drawn into. The 0.144 declared above is the maze-B, binding value. A procedure check run at finer power than the family it validates would prove nothing about that family.

positiveControl.expectedDirection: wt-doubled must be selected as the best arm in the full option set on BOTH mazes, on the primary metric hallHpAuc, at the registered split seed. Doubling the damage of the one structure every arm builds twelve of is a large, unambiguous, monotone improvement to the defence; if the argmax-over-a-noisy-set procedure cannot find it, it cannot be trusted to find anything smaller. The commitment is an ORDERING commitment (rank 1 of 8, both mazes), not a magnitude: no honest prior exists for the size of the effect in hallHpAuc units, and inventing one would be fake precision. expectedDirection rather than expectedEffect is used for exactly that reason.

regime.label: R2 (option-set procedure check)
regime.justification: Byte-for-byte the option-set-pilot regime, because a procedure check is only evidence about the procedure AS RUN on the family it validates. Any regime difference would leave open that the procedure works here and not there. R2 (spendDown, maxWaves 10) is the standing regime adopted 2026-08-15 on 18/18 gates; legacySiting false removes the Watchtower-displacement confound of docs/reviews/2026-08-16-maze-split-mechanism.md. The seven policy arms are copied unchanged from test/harness/bench/specs/option-set-pilot.json; the eighth differs from the control arm in exactly one BALANCE dial and no protocol field.
regime.scopeLimit: This family validates the SELECTION PROCEDURE and nothing else. It issues NO balance verdict: not about the seven policies, not about Magma Trap, not about Watchtower damage. wt-doubled is a balanceOverrides arm, not a strategy a player can choose, so it is not a policy and must never be added to the option-set-pilot policy set — per spec section 2.5, any non-fusion arm inside P survives every P \ X and would force every contribution estimate to zero. The seven policy arms are re-run here only to reproduce the set the procedure operates over; their numbers in this corpus MUST NOT be pooled with, or substituted for, the option-set-pilot corpus, which is a separate registration. A PASS here says the procedure can find a large planted effect at this n; it does NOT say the procedure is unbiased at small effect sizes, and it says nothing about the siting/fusion confound documented in docs/reviews/2026-08-27-option-set-pilot-result.md section 2.

decisionRule: PASS if and only if the split-sample selection procedure (spec section 2.4, analyze.mjs --option-set, at the split seed registered in the result document BEFORE analysis) selects wt-doubled as the best arm in the full option set on BOTH maze A and maze B on the primary metric hallHpAuc, AND its selection margin over the runner-up exceeds that maze's selection-half MDE so the selection is not flagged SELECTED BY NOISE. The secondary metric wavesCleared and the 200-split selection stability distribution are reported alongside but are NOT gates: stability is reported, never gated, per spec section 2.6. Selection on one maze only is a FAIL, not a partial pass. FAILURE IS A PUBLISHABLE, ACTIONABLE OUTCOME AND MUST BE PUBLISHED: per spec section 5 refutation condition (2), if this check fails then the selection procedure itself is broken and every option-set result -- including the maze-A contribution published in docs/reviews/2026-08-27-option-set-pilot-result.md -- must be treated as unread until the procedure is fixed and this family re-run. Do not reinterpret a failure as a finding about Watchtower damage.
whatWouldRefute: (1) wt-doubled is not selected as best on one or both mazes -> the selection procedure cannot recover a large planted effect and is broken; publish and fix before reading any fusion result from option-set-pilot. (2) wt-doubled is selected but its margin over the runner-up is below the selection-half MDE (the analyser prints SELECTED BY NOISE) -> the procedure found it only by luck at this n, and the pilot's n is too small for the procedure to be trusted. (3) wt-doubled is selected on both mazes but the doubled-damage arm's mean is NOT the largest in the raw descriptives table -> the split-sample machinery disagrees with the plain arm means, which would indicate a defect in splitCells or commonCells rather than a successful validation. All three registered before any run of this family. (4) ADDED BY THE 2026-08-27 AMENDMENT, BEFORE THE RE-RUN AT 3000 SEEDS: if wt-doubled is again selected on both mazes but the maze-A margin is again inside the selection-half MDE at the new n, that is NOT a further instrument defect to be fixed by yet more seeds. It would mean the true maze-A margin between the planted arm and fuse-flank is smaller than ~0.06, i.e. that doubling the damage of the structure every arm builds twelve of is worth barely more on that maze than one policy's fusion-plus-siting choice. The conclusion to publish then is that THIS OPTION SET CANNOT HAVE ITS WINNER RESOLVED ON MAZE A AT ANY PRACTICAL n, which is a finding about the design space and about the argmax estimator's usability here -- not a licence to keep raising n until it passes, and not a licence to drop an arm.
notes:
REGISTERED BEFORE ANY RUN. No record of this family existed on disk when this file was written; the sweep spec test/harness/bench/specs/option-set-procedure-check.json was authored in the same commit and had not been executed.

WHY THIS FAMILY EXISTS SEPARATELY. Spec section 2.5: the positive control must live OUTSIDE the argmax. A balanceOverrides arm is not a strategy a player can choose, so it is not a policy; and any non-fusion arm inside P survives every P \ X and forces every contribution to zero (revision 1 of the spec's fatal defect). Validate the procedure, then measure with the procedure. This file is the validation; option-set-pilot is the measurement.

CONTROL ARM NAMING. As in option-set-pilot, the spec's 'wt-free' row is named 'control' because analyze.mjs hard-codes CONTROL_ARM = 'control' (test/harness/bench/analyze.mjs:23) and this schema requires the arms list to include a literal 'control'. wt-doubled is that same control arm plus one doubled dial, so the planted effect is isolated to the dial.

familySize = 28, counted as (arms - 1) x mazes x (1 + secondaryMetrics) = 7 x 2 x 2, by the same formula option-set-pilot used to reach 24 with one fewer arm. As in that family this is deliberately over-padded relative to the number of tests --option-set actually emits, which makes every q harder to pass and therefore cannot manufacture a positive. The decision rule above is an ordering criterion and does not depend on any q, so the padding costs this family nothing.

INSTRUMENT STATE. This family is registered after the 2026-08-27 fix to stats.js signTest, which previously underflowed Math.pow(0.5, n) to zero for n > 1074 and returned p = 0 -- a free PASS on the sign gate. That defect is not in the path of this family's decision rule (an argmax ordering, not a sign test), but the corpus is taken on the fixed instrument and the fix is committed before the sweep runs, so this family's records carry a clean, non-dirty engine signature. option-set-pilot's records do not; see that result document's limits.

SEEDS. 750 seeds x 2 postGaps = 1500 cells per arm per maze, identical to option-set-pilot, giving 8 x 2 x 750 x 2 = 24,000 runs. Matching the pilot's per-cell n is the point: this check must run at the pilot's power, not better.
amendmentNote:
AMENDMENT, 2026-08-27, AFTER A REGISTERED FAILURE AND BEFORE THE RE-RUN. The first run of this family (750 seeds, 24,000 runs, corpus test/harness/store/2026-08-27-option-set-procedure-check.jsonl.gz, result docs/reviews/2026-08-27-option-set-procedure-check-result.md) FAILED the decisionRule. wt-doubled was selected on both mazes, on both metrics, on 200/200 stability splits, and held the largest raw mean on both -- so refutation (3) was clear and there is no evidence of a defect in the selection code. It failed the margin clause: on maze A it cleared the runner-up (fuse-flank) by only 0.080 against a selection-half MDE of 0.123, so the analyser flagged SELECTED BY NOISE and refutation (2) fired. THIS AMENDMENT IS THE REMEDY REFUTATION (2) PRESCRIBES, AND IS BEING MADE BECAUSE OF THAT FAILURE -- it is a re-declaration after seeing a shortfall, which is legitimate only because it is recorded as such here, before the re-run, and because it changes ONLY n. 

WHAT CHANGES: seeds 750 -> 3000 in test/harness/bench/specs/option-set-procedure-check.json (8 arms x 2 mazes x 3000 seeds x 2 postGaps = 96,000 runs). CORRECTION made before the re-run: the 24,000 runs already stored are NOT reused, even though their seeds are a strict subset. configHash includes the engine identity (record.js:78), the first corpus was taken at gitSha f1f74ab, and committing that corpus and its result moved HEAD -- so every runId differs and exact resume matches nothing. This is correct behaviour, not a defect: a record is tied to the engine that produced it. The re-run therefore writes a SEPARATE store, test/harness/store/2026-08-27-option-set-procedure-check-n3000.jsonl.gz, rather than appending two engine identities into one file where option-set mode -- which does not band by version -- would silently pool them. The 750-seed corpus is kept as the record of the failure it documents. mde 0.144 -> 0.0721 and nRequired 1506 -> 6004, both recomputed on the SAME maze-B historical sigma 1.41 at the new split-half size: mde(1.41/sqrt(2), 3000) = 0.0721, ceil(requiredN(1.41, 0.0721)) = 6004. 

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the arms, the policy set, the mazes, the regime, the metrics, the split seed (20260827, registered in the result document before the first analysis), the decisionRule, and refutation conditions (1)-(3). NOTHING IS REMOVED FROM THE OPTION SET. Narrowing the set -- dropping fuse-flank in particular -- would widen the winning margin and make this check pass trivially, and is exactly the researcher degree of freedom the split-sample design exists to remove. It is prohibited here as firmly as extending option-set-pilot's set is prohibited there. 

WHY 3000 AND NOT THE MINIMUM. The selection-half MDE is computed from observed spread and so scales as 1/sqrt(n): 0.123 x sqrt(750/3000) = 0.0615 on maze A and 0.173 x sqrt(750/3000) = 0.0865 on maze B. 3000 seeds is exactly 4x, which exactly halves both. The bare minimum to clear the observed 0.080 margin is ~1773 seeds; 3000 was chosen instead so the check is not sized to just barely pass its own point estimate, and it leaves ~23% headroom against that estimate. It is NOT sized to the lower bound of the margin's 95% CI (roughly [0.037, 0.123], from the paired delta 0.0800 at t 3.66 on n=1500), which would need ~8300 seeds and ~265,000 runs -- see refutation (4), added below, for what it means if the truth is down there.

A CONTRADICTION THIS AMENDMENT CREATES, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. sigmaSource above justifies the original 750 seeds on the grounds that 'a procedure check run at finer power than the family it validates would prove nothing about that family.' That reasoning is CORRECT and this amendment knowingly violates it, so the licence a PASS at 3000 seeds grants is correspondingly narrower and is fixed here in advance: a PASS at 3000 seeds validates the selection procedure AT 3000 SEEDS ONLY. It does NOT retroactively license reading option-set-pilot's maze-A numbers, which were taken at 750. The first run of this family already established what happens at 750 -- the procedure cannot resolve its own winner there -- and that finding is not undone by a larger re-run. CONSEQUENCE: if this re-run PASSES, option-set-pilot must ITSELF be re-run at 3000 seeds (7 arms x 2 mazes x 3000 x 2 = 84,000 runs, of which 21,000 are already stored and reused) before its maze-A estimator output may be read. Reading the 750-seed pilot on the strength of a 3000-seed procedure check would be precisely the error sigmaSource warns against.
